seo_description: Press a hotkey, drag a rectangle anywhere on screen, and your window snaps to that exact frame. Free, open-source, native window management for macOS 14+.
hero_sub: Press Command-Shift-Space, drag a freehand rectangle on any display, and the frontmost window resizes to exactly that frame. Free, native, and open source.
features_title: Sized by hand, not by grid.
features_sub: A single drag replaces layout shortcuts, with just enough magnetism to keep edges clean.

features.title: Freehand rectangle on release
features.desc: Drag anywhere on a dimmed overlay with a live label showing size in points and as a percentage of the screen. Let go and the window moves and resizes to that frame.

features.title: Soft magnetic snapping
features.desc: Edges snap to screen edges, thirds, and optional center lines within a distance you set from 0 to 30 points. Hold Option to turn magnetism off.

features.title: Global hotkey and modifiers
features.desc: The default Command-Shift-Space is rebindable in Settings. Hold Shift to keep the window's aspect ratio, and press Escape to cancel.

features.title: Works across displays
features.desc: The overlay covers every screen, and the window lands on whichever display you draw on.

features.title: Recent frames, one key away
features.desc: The last five frames are saved as percentages, so they fit any screen size. Press 1 to 5 in the overlay or choose one from the menu bar.

features.title: Careful with edge cases
features.desc: Drags under 100 points are ignored, and full-screen windows are skipped. If a window enforces its own size limits, it is centered in the rectangle you drew.

permissions_step: Grant Accessibility access when prompted, or enable SketchFrameWindow in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility.

faq.q: Is SketchFrameWindow really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, with no accounts, servers, or network code. If it saves you time, you can optionally support development through the Ko-fi button.

Only Accessibility, which is used to find the focused window and to move and resize it. It does not request Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera, or network access, and the overlay never captures your screen.
Locally on your Mac. Settings and your last five recent frames are kept in the app's UserDefaults, and nothing is sent anywhere. You can turn off or clear recent frames in Settings.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to approve it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
